messages:
maria.g: Heads-up — staging promotion blocked by deploy-bot. The tag `release-2026-03-18` resolves to a different digest than the artifact we published from CI. Looks like a tag overwrite in the registry.

deploy-bot: [automated] Promotion paused: image tag digest mismatch. expected sha256:0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8i9j found sha256:9f8e7d6c5b4a3e2f1d0c. See http://ci.internal/build/5482 for original metadata.

sam.k: Wait — was there a parallel pipeline that might have reused the tag?

maria.g: Checking logs. CI summary shows nightly-canary used the same tag pattern and pushed at 03:12 UTC, build id b589. Official release push was at 03:15 UTC, build id b592. Looks like the nightly finished slower and overwrote the tag after our release push.

jonathan: Ugh. That means the signed attestation we created is for b592 but the tag now points at b589. Cosign/attestation verification will fail and deploybot is doing the right thing.

maria.g: Repro steps I ran:
```
# AWS ECR check
aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name webapp --image-ids imageTag=release-2026-03-18 --query 'images[*].imageManifest' --output text
# result includes manifest with config.digest: sha256:9f8e7d6c5b4a3e2f1d0c
```

infra-oncall: Do we have the original digest for b592? We should pin by digest in the k8s manifests and reopen promotion only when artifact and attestation align.

sam.k: Yes, we saved the CI artifact mapping. b592 -> sha256:0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8i9j. If we retag now, we should push a new immutable tag (release-2026-03-18+build592) and re-run attestation. Avoid reusing the exact tag.

maria.g: Proposed plan: 1) Disable auto-promote for this release in deploybot (hold), 2) Create new immutable tag `release-2026-03-18-b592` pointing at sha256:0a1b2..., 3) Re-run signing/attestation job on CI, 4) Verify cosign attest and then manually trigger deploybot promote, 5) Update release notes with pinned digest and note about tagging policy change.

deploy-bot: [automated] Promotion held until manual approve. Use `/deploybot promote --manual <tag>` once attestation verifies.

jonathan: I also want to add a short-term guard in release pipeline: fail if tag already exists and points to a different digest unless `--force-retag` is provided. This will stop accidental overwrites.

infra-oncall: Agree. We should roll out that check to CI in the next 24h. For now, manual retag is safest.

maria.g: I'm starting the retag + sign job now. I'll push `release-2026-03-18-b592` and paste cosign output here. If anyone sees consumers depending on the plain `release-2026-03-18` name in staging, shout now.

sam.k: Staging apps only read the digest from the deployment controller which we pin, but double-check the k8s templating — there was an old job that used tags. I'll scan and PR any pin fixes.

maria.g: cosign verify output (initial):
```
# after re-sign
cosign verify-attestation --attestation=attestation-b592.signed webapp:release-2026-03-18-b592
Verification for webapp:release-2026-03-18-b592: OK
Predicate Type: https://in-toto.io/Statement/v0.1
Subject: sha256:0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8i9j
```

deploy-bot: [automated] Received manual promote request pending. Please confirm when ready. :eyes:

maria.g: Confirmed. I'm triggering `/deploybot promote release-2026-03-18-b592 --manual` now. Will watch canary for 10m and rollback if any error.

jonathan: Also creating a quick changelog PR to document we no longer reuse bare date tags and to recommend `+build` suffixes or digests.

infra-oncall: Follow-up action items: - CI: add tag-exists-and-diff check (24h), - Releases: avoid reusing short date tags, - Deploybot: show digest in promotion UI.

maria.g: Action note for ops: I'll update the release notes with the pinned digest and link to this thread. If canary is green at 03:45 UTC we'll proceed to full staging promote.

sam.k: Thanks. Good catch by deploy-bot. :thumbsup:
